entries.d418d1d55c48951385463a60ebc27f38502dba0a: <div sID="gen18622" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="13" osisID="Ezek.13" sID="Ezek.13"/> <div eID="gen18622" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18623" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen18624" type="x-p"/> Mention had been made, in the chapter before, of the vain visions and flattering divinations with which the people of Israel suffered themselves to be imposed upon (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.24">ver. 24</reference>); now this whole chapter is levelled against them. God's faithful prophets are nowhere so sharp upon any sort of sinners as upon the false prophets, not because they were the most spiteful enemies to them, but because they put the highest affront upon God and did the greatest mischief to his people. The prophet here shows the sin and punishment, I. Of the false prophets, <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.1-Ezek.13.16">ver. 1-16</reference>. II. Of the false prophetesses, <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.17-Ezek.13.23">ver. 17-23</reference>. Both agreed to sooth men up in their sins, and, under pretence of comforting God's people, to flatter them with hopes that they should yet have peace; but the prophets shall be proved liars, their prophecies mere shams, and the expectations of the people illusions; for God will let them know that "the deceived and the deceiver are his," are both accountable to him, <reference osisRef="Job.12.16">Job xii. 16</reference>.
entries.80647fff46788840f49cd6a17fecbbe7ac3770a7: <div eID="gen18624" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen18623" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Guilt of False Prophets. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 593.)</title> <div sID="gen18625" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And the word of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> came unto me, saying, <hi type="super">2</hi> Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy, and say thou unto them that prophesy out of their own hearts, Hear ye the word of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> ; <hi type="super">3</hi> Thus saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> ; Woe unto the foolish prophets, that follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing! <hi type="super">4</hi> O Israel, thy prophets are like the foxes in the deserts. <hi type="super">5</hi> Ye have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">6</hi> They have seen vanity and lying divination, saying, The <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> saith: and the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> hath not sent them: and they have made <hi type="italic">others</hi> to hope that they would confirm the word. <hi type="super">7</hi> Have ye not seen a vain vision, and have ye not spoken a lying divination, whereas ye say, The <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> saith <hi type="italic">it;</hi> albeit I have not spoken? <hi type="super">8</hi> Therefore thus saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> ; Because ye have spoken vanity, and seen lies, therefore, behold, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> against you, saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> . <hi type="super">9</hi> And mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies: they shall not be in the assembly of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel; and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> . <div eID="gen18625" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18626" type="x-p"/> The false prophets, who are here prophesied against, were some of them at Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Jer.23.14">Jer. xxiii. 14</reference>): <hi type="italic">I have seen in the prophets at Jerusalem a horrible thing;</hi> some of them among the captives in Babylon, for to them Jeremiah writes (<reference osisRef="Jer.29.8">Jer. xxix. 8</reference>), <hi type="italic">Let not your diviners, that be in the midst of you, deceive you.</hi> And as God's prophets, though at a distance from each other in place or time, yet preached the same truths, which was an evidence that they were guided by one and the same good Spirit, so the false prophets prophesied the same lies, being actuated by one and the same spirit of error. There were little hopes of bringing them to repentance, they were so hardened in their sin; yet Ezekiel must prophesy against them, in hopes that the people might be cautioned not to hearken to them; and thus a testimony will be left upon record against them, and they will thereby be left inexcusable. <div eID="gen18626" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18627" type="x-p"/> Ezekiel had express orders to <hi type="italic">prophesy against the prophets of Israel;</hi> so they called themselves, as if none but they had been worthy of the name of Israel's prophets, who were indeed Israel's deceivers. But it is observable that Israel was never imposed upon by pretenders to prophecy till after they had rejected and abused the true prophets; as, afterwards, they were never deluded by counterfeit messiahs till after they had refused the true Messiah and rejected him. These false prophets must be required to <hi type="italic">hear the word of the Lord.</hi> They took upon them to speak what concerned others as from God; let them now hear what concerned themselves as from him. And two things the prophet is directed to do:— <div eID="gen18627" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18628" type="x-p"/> I. To discover their sin to them, and to convince them of that if possible, or thereby to prevent their proceeding any further, by making <hi type="italic">manifest their folly unto all men,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Tim.3.9">2 Tim. iii. 9</reference>. They are here called <hi type="italic">foolish prophets</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.3">v. 3</reference>), men that did not at all understand the business they pretended to; to make fools of the people they made fools of themselves, and put the greatest cheat upon their own souls. Let us see what is here laid to their charge. 1. They pretend to have a commission from God, whereas he never sent them. They thrust themselves into the prophetic office, without warrant from him who is <hi type="italic">the Lord God</hi> of the holy prophets, which was a foolish thing; for how could they expect that God should own them in a work to which he never called them? They are <hi type="italic">prophets out of their own hearts</hi> (so the margin reads it, <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.2">v. 2</reference>), prophets of their own making, <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.6">v. 6</reference>. <hi type="italic">They say, The Lord saith;</hi> they pretend to be his messengers, but <hi type="italic">the Lord has not sent them,</hi> has not given them any orders. They counterfeit the broad seal of heaven, than which they cannot do a greater indignity to mankind, for hereby they put a reproach upon divine revelation, lessen its credit, and weaken its credibility. When these pretenders are found to be deceivers, atheists and infidels will thence infer, They are all so. <hi type="italic">The Lord has not sent them;</hi> for though crafty enough in other things <hi type="italic">like the foxes,</hi> and very wise for the world, yet they are <hi type="italic">foolish prophets</hi> and have no experimental acquaintance with the things of God. Note, Foolish prophets are not of God's sending, for whom he sends he either finds fit or makes fit. Where he gives warrant he gives wisdom. 2. They pretend to have instructions from God, whereas he never made himself and his mind known to them: <hi type="italic">They followed their own spirit</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.3">v. 3</reference>); they delivered that as a message from God which was the product either of their subtle invention, to serve a turn for themselves, or of their own crazed and heated imagination, to give vent to a fancy. For <hi type="italic">they have seen nothing,</hi> they have not really had any heavenly vision; they pretend that what they say <hi type="italic">the Lord saith it,</hi> but God disowns it: "<hi type="italic">I have not spoken it,</hi> I never said it, never meant any such thing." What they delivered was not what they had seen or heard, as that is which the ministers of Christ deliver (<reference osisRef="1John.1.1">1 John i. 1</reference>), but either what they had dreamed or what they thought would please those they coveted to make an interest in; this is called their <hi type="italic">seeing vanity and lying divination</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.6">v. 6</reference>); they pretended to have seen that which they did not see, and produced that as a divine truth which they knew to be false. To the same purport (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.7">v. 7</reference>): <hi type="italic">You have see a vain vision and spoken a lying divination,</hi> which had no divine original and would have no effect, but would certainly be disproved by the event; the words are changed (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.8">v. 8</reference>): <hi type="italic">You have spoken vanity and seen lies;</hi> what they saw and what they said was all alike, a mere sham; they saw nothing, they said nothing, to the purpose, nothing that could be relied on or that deserved regard. Again (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.9">v. 9</reference>), They <hi type="italic">see vanity and divine lies;</hi> they pretended to have had visions, as the true prophets had, whereas really they had none, but either it was the creature of their own fancy (they thought they had a vision, as men in a delirium do, that was <hi type="italic">seeing vanity</hi>) or it was a fiction of their own politics, and they knew they had none, and then they <hi type="italic">saw lies, and divined lies.</hi> See <reference osisRef="Jer.23.16">Jer. xxiii. 16</reference>, &c. Note, Since the devil is universally know to be the father of lies, those put the highest affront imaginable upon God who tell lies, and then father them upon him. But those that had put God's character upon Satan, in worshipping devils, arrived at length at such a pitch of impiety as to put Satan's character upon God. 3. They took no care to prevent the judgments of God that were breaking in upon the kingdom. They are like <hi type="italic">the foxes in the deserts,</hi> running to and fro, and seeming to be in a great hurry, but it was to get away and shift for their own safety, not to do any good: <hi type="italic">The hireling flees, and leaves the sheep.</hi> They are like foxes that are greedy of prey for themselves, crafty and cruel to feed themselves. But (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.5">v. 5</reference>), "You <hi type="italic">have not gone up into the gaps, nor made up the hedge of the house of Israel.</hi> A breach is made in their fences, at which judgments are ready to pour in upon them, and then, if ever, is the time to do them service; but you have done nothing to help them." They should have made intercession for them, to turn away the wrath of God; but they were not praying prophets, had no interest in heaven nor intercourse with heaven (as prophets used to have, <reference osisRef="Gen.20.7">Gen. xx. 7</reference>) and so could do them no service that way. They should have made it their business by preaching and advice to bring people to repentance and reformation, and so have <hi type="italic">made up the hedge,</hi> and put a stop to the judgments of God; but this was none of their care: they contrived how to pleased people, not how to profit them. They saw a deluge of profaneness and impiety breaking in upon the land, waging war with virtue and holiness, and threatening to crush them and bear them down, and then they should have come in <hi type="italic">to the help of the Lord, to the help of the Lord against the mighty,</hi> by witnessing against the wickedness of the time and place they lived in; but they thought that would be as dangerous a piece of service as standing in a breach to make it good against the besiegers, and therefore they declined it, did nothing to stem the tide, stood not in the battle against vice and immorality, but basely deserted the cause of religion and reformation, <hi type="italic">in the day of the Lord,</hi> when it was proclaimed, <hi type="italic">Who is on the Lord's side? Who will rise up for me against the evil-doers?</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.94.16">Ps. xciv. 16</reference>. Those were unworthy the name of prophets that could think so favourably of sin, and had so little zeal for God and the public welfare. 4. They flattered people into a vain hope that the judgments God had threatened would never come, whereby they hardened those in sin whom they should have endeavoured to turn from sin (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.6">v. 6</reference>): <hi type="italic">They have made others to hope</hi> that all should be well, and they should have peace, though they went on still in their trespasses, and that the event would confirm the word. They were still ready to say, "We will warrant you that these troubles will be at an end quickly, and we shall be in prosperity again." as if their warrants would confirm false prophecies, in defiance of God himself. <div eID="gen18628" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18629" type="x-p"/> II. He is directed to denounce the judgments of God against them for these sins, from which their pretending to the character of prophets would not exempt them. 1. In general, here is a <hi type="italic">woe</hi> against them (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.3">v. 3</reference>), and what that woe is we are told (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.8">v. 8</reference>). <hi type="italic">Behold, I am against you, saith the Lord God.</hi> Note, Those are in a woeful condition that have God against them. Woe, and a thousand woes, to those that have made him their enemy. 2. In particular, they are sentenced to be excluded from all the privileges of the commonwealth of Israel, for they are adjudged to have forfeited them all (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.9">v. 9</reference>): God's <hi type="italic">hand shall be upon them,</hi> to seize them and bring them to his bar, to shut them out from his presence, and they will find it a <hi type="italic">fearful thing to fall into his hands.</hi> They pretend to be prophets, particular favourites of heaven, and authorized to preside in the congregation of his church on earth; but, by pretending to the honours they were not entitled to, they lost those that otherwise they might have enjoyed, <reference osisRef="Matt.5.19">Matt. v. 19</reference>. Their doom is, (1.) To be expelled from the communion of saints, and not to be looked upon as belonging to it: <hi type="italic">They shall not be in the secret of my people;</hi> their folly shall be so clearly manifested that they shall never be consulted, nor their advice asked; they shall not be present at any debates about public affairs. Or, rather, they shall not be in the assembly of God's people for religious worship, for they shall be ashamed to show their heads there, when they are proved by the events to be false prophets, and, like Cain, shall <hi type="italic">go out from the presence of the Lord.</hi> The people that are deceived by them shall abandon them, and resolve to have no more to do with them. Those that usurped Moses's chair shall not be allowed so much as a door-keeper's place. In the great day they shall <hi type="italic">not stand in the congregation of the righteous</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.1.5">Ps. i. 5</reference>), when God <hi type="italic">gathers his saints together to him</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.50.5">Ps. l. 5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.50.16">16</reference>), <hi type="italic">to be for ever with him.</hi> (2.) To be expunged out of the book of the living. They shall die in their captivity, and shall die childless, shall leave no posterity to take their denomination from them, and so their names shall not be found among those who either themselves or their posterity returned out of Babylon, of whom a particular account was kept in a public register, which was called <hi type="italic">the writing of the house of Israel,</hi> such as we have <reference osisRef="Ezra.2.1-Ezra.2.70">Ezra ii.</reference> They shall not be found among the living in Jerusalem, <reference osisRef="Isa.4.3">Isa. iv. 3</reference>. Or they shall not be found written among those whom God has from eternity chosen to be vessels of his mercy to eternity. We read of those who <hi type="italic">prophesied in Christ's name,</hi> and yet he will tell them that he <hi type="italic">never knew them</hi> (<reference osisRef="Matt.7.22-Matt.7.23">Matt. vii. 22, 23</reference>), because they were not among those that were <hi type="italic">given to him.</hi> The Chaldee paraphrase reads it, <hi type="italic">They shall not be written in the writing of eternal life, which is written for the righteous of the house of Israel.</hi> See <reference osisRef="Ps.69.28">Ps. lxix. 28</reference>. (3.) To be for ever excluded from the land of Israel. God has <hi type="italic">sworn in his wrath</hi> concerning them that <hi type="italic">they shall never enter</hi> with the returning captives into the land of Canaan, which a second time remains a rest for them. Note, Those who oppose the design of God's threatenings, and will not be awed and influenced by them, forfeit the benefit of his promises, and cannot expect to be comforted and encouraged by them.
entries.74fe1288586a50d4e0e72183a83ae1aa648b51f5: <div eID="gen18629" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Punishment of False Prophets; The Doom of False Prophets. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 593.)</title> <div sID="gen18630" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">10</hi> Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and <hi type="italic">there was</hi> no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered <hi type="italic">mortar:</hi> <hi type="super">11</hi> Say unto them which daub <hi type="italic">it</hi> with untempered <hi type="italic">mortar,</hi> that it shall fall: there shall be an overflowing shower; and ye, O great hailstones, shall fall; and a stormy wind shall rend <hi type="italic">it.</hi> <hi type="super">12</hi> Lo, when the wall is fallen, shall it not be said unto you, Where <hi type="italic">is</hi> the daubing wherewith ye have daubed <hi type="italic">it?</hi> <hi type="super">13</hi> Therefore thus saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> ; I will even rend <hi type="italic">it</hi> with a stormy wind in my fury; and there shall be an overflowing shower in mine anger, and great hailstones in <hi type="italic">my</hi> fury to consume <hi type="italic">it.</hi> <hi type="super">14</hi> So will I break down the wall that ye have daubed with untempered <hi type="italic">mortar,</hi> and bring it down to the ground, so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall, and ye shall be consumed in the midst thereof: and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">15</hi> Thus will I accomplish my wrath upon the wall, and upon them that have daubed it with untempered <hi type="italic">mortar,</hi> and will say unto you, The wall <hi type="italic">is</hi> no <hi type="italic">more,</hi> neither they that daubed it; <hi type="super">16</hi> <hi type="italic">To wit,</hi> the prophets of Israel which prophesy concerning Jerusalem, and which see visions of peace for her, and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no peace, saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> . <div eID="gen18630" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18631" type="x-p"/> We have here more plain dealing with the false prophets, and some further articles of their doom. We have seen the people made ashamed of the false prophets (though sometimes they had been fond of them) and casting them away, as they shall do their false gods, with indignation; now here we find them as much ashamed of their false prophecies, which they had sometimes depended upon with much assurance. Observe, <div eID="gen18631" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18632" type="x-p"/> I. How the people are deceived by the false prophets. Those flatterers seduce them, saying, <hi type="italic">Peace, and there was no peace,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.10">v. 10</reference>. They pretended to have <hi type="italic">seen visions of peace,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.16">v. 16</reference>. But that could not be, for <hi type="italic">there was no peace, saith the Lord God.</hi> There was no prosperity designed for them, and therefore there could be no ground for their security; yet they told them that God was at peace with them, and had mercy in reserve for them, and that the war they were engaged in with the Chaldeans should soon end in an honourable peace, and their land should enjoy a happy repose and tranquillity. They told the idolaters and other sinners that there was neither harm nor danger in the way they were in. Thus they <hi type="italic">seduced God's people;</hi> they put a cheat upon them, led them into mistakes, and drew them aside out of that way of repentance and reformation which the other prophets were endeavouring to bring them into. Note, Those are the most dangerous seducers who suggest to sinners that which tends to lessen their dread of sin and their fear of God. Now this is compared to the building of a slight rotten wall, or, according to our Saviour's similitude, which is to the same purport with this (<reference osisRef="Matt.7.26">Matt. vii. 26</reference>), the <hi type="italic">building of a house upon the sand,</hi> which seems to be a shelter and protection for a while, but will fall when a storm comes. One false prophet built the wall, set up the notion that God was not at all displeased with Jerusalem, but that the city should be confirmed in its flourishing state, and be victorious over the powers that now threatened it. This notion was very pleasing, and he that started it made himself very acceptable by it and was caressed by every body, which invited others to say the same. They made the matter look yet more plausible and promising; they <hi type="italic">daubed the wall,</hi> which the first had built, but it was with <hi type="italic">untempered mortar,</hi> sorry stuff, that will not bind nor hold the bricks together; they had no ground for what they said, nor had it any consistency with itself, but was like ropes of sand. They did not strengthen the wall, were in no care to make it firm, to see that they went upon sure grounds; they only daubed it to hide the cracks and make it look well to the eye. And the wall thus built, when it comes to any stress, much more to any distress, will bulge and totter, and come down by degrees. Note, Doctrines that are groundless, though ever so grateful, that are not built upon a scripture foundation nor fastened with a scripture cement, though ever so plausible, ever so pleasing, are not of any worth, nor will stand men in any stead; and those hopes of peace and happiness which are not warranted by the word of God will but cheat men, like a wall that is well daubed indeed, but ill-built. <div eID="gen18632" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18633" type="x-p"/> II. How they will be soon undeceived by the judgment of God, which, we are sure, is according to truth. 1. God will in anger bring a terrible storm that shall beat fiercely and furiously upon the wall. The descent which the Chaldean army shall make upon Judah, and the siege which they shall lay to Jerusalem, will be as <hi type="italic">an overflowing shower,</hi> or inundation (such as Solomon calls a <hi type="italic">sweeping rain that leaves no food,</hi> <reference osisRef="Prov.28.3">Prov. xxviii. 3</reference>), will bear down all before it, as the deluge did in Noah's time: <hi type="italic">You, O great hailstones! shall fall,</hi> the artillery of heaven, every hailstone like a cannon-ball, battering this wall, and with these a <hi type="italic">stormy wind,</hi> which is sometimes so strong as to <hi type="italic">rend the rocks</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.19.11">1 Kings xix. 11</reference>), much more an ill-built wall, <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.11">v. 11</reference>. But that which makes this <hi type="italic">rain,</hi> and <hi type="italic">hail,</hi> and <hi type="italic">wind,</hi> most terrible is that they arise from the wrath of God, and are enforced by that; it is that which sends them; it is that which gives them the setting on (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.13">v. 13</reference>); it is <hi type="italic">a stormy wind in my fury,</hi> and <hi type="italic">an overflowing shower in my anger,</hi> and <hi type="italic">great hailstones in my fury.</hi> The fury of Nebuchadnezzar and his princes, who highly resented Zedekiah's treachery, made the invasion very formidable, but that was nothing in comparison with God's displeasure. <hi type="italic">The staff in their hand is my indignation,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.10.5">Isa. x. 5</reference>. Note, An angry God has winds and storms at command wherewith to alarm secure sinners; and his wrath makes them frightful and forcible indeed; for <hi type="italic">who can stand before him when he is angry?</hi> 2. This storm shall overturn the wall: <hi type="italic">it shall fall,</hi> and the wind shall <hi type="italic">rend it</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.11">v. 11</reference>), the <hi type="italic">hailstones shall consume it</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.13">v. 13</reference>); I will <hi type="italic">break it down</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.14">v. 14</reference>) and <hi type="italic">bring it to the ground,</hi> so that the <hi type="italic">foundation thereof shall be discovered;</hi> it will appear how false, how rotten it was, to the prophetical reproach of the builders. When the Chaldean army has made Judah and Jerusalem desolate then this credit of the prophets, and the hopes of the people, will both sink together; the former will be found false in flattering the people and the latter foolish in suffering themselves to be imposed upon by them, and so exposed to so much the greater confusion, when the judgment shall surprise them in their security. Note, Whatever men think to shelter themselves with against the judgments of God, while they continue unreformed, will prove but a <hi type="italic">refuge of lies</hi> and will not profit them <hi type="italic">in the day of wrath.</hi> See <reference osisRef="Isa.28.17">Isa. xxviii. 17</reference>. Men's anger cannot shake that which God has built (for <hi type="italic">the blast of the terrible ones is but as a storm against the wall,</hi> which makes a great noise, but never stirs the wall; see <reference osisRef="Isa.25.4">Isa. xxv. 4</reference>), but God's anger will overthrow that which men have built in opposition to him. They and all their attempts, they and all the securities wherein they intrench themselves, shall be <hi type="italic">as a bowing wall and as a tottering fence</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.62.3">Ps. lxii. 3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.62.10">10</reference>); and when their vain predictions are disproved, and their vain expectations disappointed, then it will be discovered that there was no ground for either, <reference osisRef="Hab.3.13">Hab. iii. 13</reference>. The <hi type="italic">day will declare</hi> what every man's work is, and <hi type="italic">the fire will try</hi> it, <reference osisRef="1Cor.3.13">1 Cor. iii. 13</reference>. 3. The builders of the wall, and those that daubed it, will themselves be buried in the ruins of it: <hi type="italic">It shall fall, and you shall</hi> be <hi type="italic">consumed in the midst thereof,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.14">v. 14</reference>. And thus the threatenings of God's wrath, and all the just intentions of it, shall be accomplished to the uttermost, both upon <hi type="italic">the wall</hi> and upon those <hi type="italic">that have daubed it,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.15">v. 15</reference>. The same judgments that will prove the false prophets to be false will punish them for their falsehood; and they themselves shall be involved in the calamity which they made the people believe there was no danger of, and become monuments of that justice which they bade defiance to. Thus, if <hi type="italic">the blind lead the blind,</hi> both the blind leaders and the blind followers will <hi type="italic">fall together into the ditch.</hi> Note, Those that deceive others will in the end prove to have deceived themselves; and no doom will be more fearful than that of unfaithful ministers, that flattered sinners in their sins. 4. Both the deceivers and the deceived, when they thus perish together, will justly be ridiculed and triumphed over (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.12">v. 12</reference>): <hi type="italic">When the wall has fallen shall it not be said unto you,</hi> by those that gave credit to the true prophets, and feared the word of the Lord, "Now <hi type="italic">where is the daubing wherewith you have daubed the wall?</hi> What has become of all the fine soft words and fair promises wherewith you flattered your wicked neighbours, and all the assurances you gave them that the troubles of the nation should soon be at an end?" The <hi type="italic">righteous shall laugh at them,</hi> the righteous God shall, righteous men shall, saying, <hi type="italic">Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.52.6-Ps.52.7">Ps. lii. 6, 7</reference>. <hi type="italic">I also will laugh at your calamity,</hi> <reference osisRef="Prov.1.26">Prov. i. 26</reference>. They will say unto you (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.15">v. 15</reference>), "<hi type="italic">The wall is no more, neither he that daubed it;</hi> your hopes have vanished, and those that supported them, even <hi type="italic">the prophets of Israel,</hi>" <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.16">v. 16</reference>. Note, Those that usurp the honours that do not belong to them will shortly be filled with the shame that does.
entries.9e27ca4fdab30b1833074bd7d7938e94fabcdae2: <div eID="gen18633" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Guilt of the False Prophetesses. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 593.)</title> <div sID="gen18634" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">17</hi> Likewise, thou son of man, set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesy out of their own heart; and prophesy thou against them, <hi type="super">18</hi> And say, Thus saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> ; Woe to the <hi type="italic">women</hi> that sew pillows to all armholes, and make kerchiefs upon the head of every stature to hunt souls! Will ye hunt the souls of my people, and will ye save the souls alive <hi type="italic">that come</hi> unto you? <hi type="super">19</hi> And will ye pollute me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to slay the souls that should not die, and to save the souls alive that should not live, by your lying to my people that hear <hi type="italic">your</hi> lies? <hi type="super">20</hi> Wherefore thus saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> ; Behold, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> against your pillows, wherewith ye there hunt the souls to make <hi type="italic">them</hi> fly, and I will tear them from your arms, and will let the souls go, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the souls that ye hunt to make <hi type="italic">them</hi> fly. <hi type="super">21</hi> Your kerchiefs also will I tear, and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand to be hunted; and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">22</hi> Because with lies ye have made the heart of the righteous sad, whom I have not made sad; and strengthened the hands of the wicked, that he should not return from his wicked way, by promising him life: <hi type="super">23</hi> Therefore ye shall see no more vanity, nor divine divinations: for I will deliver my people out of your hand: and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <div eID="gen18634" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18635" type="x-p"/> As God has promised that when he pours out his Spirit upon his people both <hi type="italic">their sons and their daughters shall prophesy,</hi> so the devil, when he acts as a spirit of lies and falsehood, is so in the mouth not only of false prophets, but of false prophetesses too, and those are the deceivers whom the prophet is here directed to prophesy against; for they are not such despicable enemies to God's truths as deserve not to be taken notice of, nor yet will either the weakness of their sex excuse their sin or the tenderness and respect that are owing to it exempt them from the reproaches and threatenings of the word of God. No: <hi type="italic">Son of man, set they face against the daughters of thy people,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.17">v. 17</reference>. God takes no pleasure in owning them for his people. They are <hi type="italic">thy people,</hi> as <reference osisRef="Exod.32.7">Exod. xxxii. 7</reference>. The women pretend to a spirit of prophecy, and are in the same song with the men, as Ahab's prophets were: <hi type="italic">Go on, and prosper.</hi> They <hi type="italic">prophesy out of their own heart</hi> too; they say what comes uppermost and what they know nothing of. Therefore <hi type="italic">prophesy against them</hi> from God's own mouth. The prophet must <hi type="italic">set his face against them,</hi> and try if they can look him in the face and stand to what they say. Note, When sinners grow very impudent it is time for reprovers to be very bold. Now observe, <div eID="gen18635" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18636" type="x-p"/> I. How the sin of these false prophetesses is described, and what are the particulars of it. 1. They told deliberate lies to those who consulted them, and came to them to be advised, and to be told their fortune: "You do mischief <hi type="italic">by your lying to my people that hear your lies</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.19">v. 19</reference>); they come to be told the truth, but you tell them lies; and, because you humour them in their sins, they are willing to hear you." Note, It is ill with those people who can better hear pleasing lies than unpleasing truths; and it is a temptation to those who lie in wait to deceive to tell lies when they find people willing to hear them and to excuse themselves with this, <hi type="italic">Si populus vult decipi, decipiatur—If the people will be deceived, let them.</hi> 2. They profaned the name of God by pretending to have received those lies from him (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.19">v. 19</reference>): "<hi type="italic">You pollute my name among my people,</hi> and make use of that for the patronising of your lies and the gaining of credit to them." Note, Those greatly pollute God's holy name that make use of it to give countenance to falsehood and wickedness. Yet this they did <hi type="italic">for handfuls of barley and pieces of bread.</hi> They did it for gain; they cared not what dishonour they did to God's name by their lying, so they could but make a hand of it for themselves. There is nothing so sacred which men of mercenary spirits, in whom the love of this world reigns, will not profane and prostitute, if they can but get money by the bargain. But they did it for poor gain; if they could get no more for it, rather than break they would sell you a false prophecy that should please you to a nicety for the beggar's dole, a <hi type="italic">piece of bread</hi> or <hi type="italic">a handful of barley;</hi> and yet that was more than it was worth. Had they asked it as an alms, for God's sake, surely they might have had it, and God would have been honoured; but, taking it as a fee for a false prophecy, God's name if polluted, and the smallness of the reward heightens the offence. <hi type="italic">For a piece of bread that man will transgress,</hi> <reference osisRef="Prov.28.21">Prov. xxviii. 21</reference>. Had their poverty been their temptation to <hi type="italic">steal, and so to take the name of the Lord in vain,</hi> it would not have been nearly so bad as when it tempted them to <hi type="italic">prophesy lies in his name</hi> and so to profane it. 3. They kept people in awe, and terrified them with their pretensions: "<hi type="italic">You hunt the souls of my people</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.18">v. 18</reference>), <hi type="italic">hunt them to make them flee</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.20">v. 20</reference>), <hi type="italic">hunt them into gardens</hi> (so the margin reads it); you use all the arts you have to court or compel them into those places where you deliver your pretended predictions, or you have got such an influence upon them that you make them do just as you would have them to do, and tyrannise over them." It was indeed the people's fault that they did regard them, but it was their fault by lies and falsehoods to command that regard; they pretended to <hi type="italic">save the souls alive that came to them,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.18">v. 18</reference>. If they would but be hearers of them, and contributors to them, they might be sure of salvation; thus they beguiled unstable souls that had a concern about salvation as their end but did not rightly understand the way, and therefore hearkened to those who were most confident in promising it to them. "But will you pretend to save souls, or secure salvation to your party?" Those are justly suspected that make such pretensions. 4. They discouraged those that were honest and good, and encouraged those that were wicked and profane: <hi type="italic">You slay the souls that should not die, and save those alive that should not live,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.19">v. 19</reference>. This is explained (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.22">v. 22</reference>): <hi type="italic">You have made the heart of the righteous sad, whom I have not made sad;</hi> because they would not, they durst not, countenance your pretensions, you thundered out the judgments of God against them, to their great grief and trouble; you put them under invidious characters, to make them either despicable or odious to the people, and pretended to do it in God's name, which made them go many a time with a sad heart; whereas it was the will of God that they should be comforted, and by having respect put upon them should have encouragement given them. But on the other side, and which is still worse, you have <hi type="italic">strengthened the hands of the wicked</hi> and emboldened them to go on in their <hi type="italic">wicked ways</hi> and not to return from them, which was the thing the true prophets with earnestness called them to. "You have promised sinners life in their sinful ways, have told them that they shall have peace though they go on, by which their <hi type="italic">hands have been strengthened</hi> and their hearts hardened." Some think this refers to the severe censures they passed upon those who had already gone into captivity (who were humbled under their affliction, by <hi type="italic">which their hearts were made sad</hi>), and the commendations they gave to those who rebelled against the king of Babylon, who were hardened in their impieties, by which their <hi type="italic">hands were strengthened;</hi> or by their polluting the name of God they saddened the hearts of good people who have a value and veneration for the word of God, and confirmed atheists and infidels in their contempt of divine revelation and furnished them with arguments against it. Note, Those have a great deal to answer for who grieve the spirits, and weaken the hands, of good people, and who gratify the lusts of sinners, and animate them in their opposition to God and religion. Nor can any thing strengthen the hands of sinners more than to tell them that they may be saved in their sins without repentance, or that there may be repentance though they do not return from their wicked ways. 5. They mimicked the true prophets, by giving signs for the illustrating of their false predictions (as Hananiah did, <reference osisRef="Jer.28.10">Jer. xxviii. 10</reference>), and they were signs agreeable to their sex; they <hi type="italic">sewed little pillows to the people's arm-holes,</hi> to signify that they might be easy and repose themselves, and needed not be disquieted with the apprehensions of trouble approaching. And they <hi type="italic">made kerchiefs upon the head of every stature,</hi> of persons of every age, young and old, distinguishable by their stature, <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.18">v. 18</reference>. These kerchiefs were badges of liberty or triumph, intimating that they should not only be delivered from the Chaldeans, but be victorious over them. Some think these were some superstitious rites which they used with those to whom they delivered their divinations, preparing them for the reception of them by putting enchanted pillows under their arms and handkerchiefs on their heads, to raise their fancies and their expectations of something great. Or perhaps the expressions are figurative: they did all they could to make people secure, which is signified by laying them easy, and to make people proud, which is signified by dressing them fine with handkerchiefs, perhaps laid or embroidered on their heads. <div eID="gen18636" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18637" type="x-p"/> II. How the wrath of God against them is expressed. Here is a woe to them (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.18">v. 18</reference>), and God declares himself against the methods they took to delude and deceive, <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.20">v. 20</reference>. But what course will God take with them? 1. They shall be confounded in their attempts, and shall proceed no further; for (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.23">v. 23</reference>) you shall <hi type="italic">see no more vanity nor divine revelations;</hi> not that they shall themselves lay down their pretensions in a way of repentance, but when the event gives them the lie they shall be silent for shame; or their fancies and imaginations shall not be disposed to receive impressions which assist them in their divinations as they have been; or they themselves shall be cut off. 2. God's people shall be delivered out of their hands. When they see themselves deluded by them into a false peace and a fool's paradise, and that though they would not leave their sin their sin has left them, and they <hi type="italic">see no more vanity nor divine divinations,</hi> they shall turn their back upon them, shall slight their predictions. The righteous shall be no more saddened by them, no, nor the wicked strengthened: The <hi type="italic">pillows shall be torn from their arms,</hi> and the <hi type="italic">kerchiefs from their heads;</hi> the fallacies shall be discovered, their frauds detected, and the people of God shall no more be in their hand, to be hunted as they had been. Note, It is a great mercy to be delivered from a servile regard to, and fear of, those who, under colour of a divine authority, impose upon and tyrannise over the consciences of men, and say to their souls, <hi type="italic">Bow down, that we may go over.</hi> But it is a sore grief to those who delight in such usurpations to have their power broken and the prey delivered; such was the reformation to the church of Rome. And, when God does this, he makes it to appear that he is the Lord, that it is his prerogative to give law to souls.  <chapter eID="Ezek.13"/> <div eID="gen18637" type="x-p"/>

entries.6094eb83b4249b27fa5e23507a2aca04718917ec: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11159"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 13</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ezek.13.1-Ezek.13.23">Eze 13:1-23</reference>. Denunciation of False Prophets and Prophetesses; Their False Teachings, and God's Consequent Judgments.</title> <div sID="gen20118" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11159"/>1. As the twelfth chapter denounced the false expectations of the people, so this denounces the false leaders who fed those expectations. As an independent witness, Ezekiel confirms at the Chebar the testimony of Jeremiah (<reference osisRef="Jer.29.21">Jr 29:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.29.31">31</reference>) in his letter from Jerusalem to the captive exiles, against the false prophets; of these some were conscious knaves, others fanatical dupes of their own frauds; for example, Ahab, Zedekiah, and Shemaiah. Hananiah must have believed his own lie, else he would not have specified so circumstantial details (<reference osisRef="Jer.28.2-Jer.28.4">Jr 28:2-4</reference>). The conscious knaves gave only general assurances of peace (<reference osisRef="Jer.5.31">Jr 5:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.6.14">6:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.14.13">14:13</reference>). The language of Ezekiel has plain references to the similar language of Jeremiah (for example, <reference osisRef="Jer.23.9-Jer.23.38">Jr 23:9-38</reference>); the bane of false prophecy, which had its stronghold in Jerusalem, having in some degree extended to the Chebar; this chapter, therefore, is primarily intended as a message to those still in the Jewish metropolis; and, secondarily, for the good of the exiles at the Chebar. <div eID="gen20118" type="x-p"/>
entries.56ca70cae15b5bd6f7e1d6c6e56571a5aeb36709: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11160"/><div sID="gen20119" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11160"/><hi type="bold">2. that prophesy--</hi>namely, a speedy return to Jerusalem.<div eID="gen20119" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20120" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">out of ... own hearts--</hi>alluding to the words of Jeremiah (<reference osisRef="Jer.23.16">Jr 23:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.23.26">26</reference>); that is, what they prophesied was what they and the people wished; the wish was father to the thought. The people wished to be deceived, and so were deceived. They were inexcusable, for they had among them true prophets (who spoke not their own thoughts, but as they were moved by the Holy Ghost, <reference osisRef="2Pet.1.21">2Pe 1:21</reference>), whom they might have known to be such, but they did not wish to know (<reference osisRef="John.3.19">Joh 3:19</reference>). <div eID="gen20120" type="x-p"/>
entries.b52737eb6c64b9285559d05aa7e608442cb53c17: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11161"/><div sID="gen20121" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11161"/><hi type="bold">3. foolish--</hi>though vaunting as though exclusively possessing "wisdom" (<reference osisRef="1Cor.1.19-1Cor.1.21">1Co 1:19-21</reference>); the fear of God being the only beginning of wisdom (<reference osisRef="Ps.111.10">Psa 111:10</reference>).<div eID="gen20121" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20122" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their own spirit--</hi>instead of the Spirit of God. A threefold distinction lay between the false and the true prophets: (1) The source of their messages respectively; of the false, "their own hearts"; of the true, an object presented to the spiritual sense (named from the noblest of the senses, a seeing) by the Spirit of God as from without, not produced by their own natural powers of reflection. The word, the body of the thought, presented itself not audibly to the natural sense, but directly to the spirit of the prophet; and so the perception of it is properly called a seeing, he perceiving that which thereafter forms itself in his soul as the cover of the external word [Delitzsch]; hence the peculiar expression, "seeing the word of God" (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.1">Is 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.13.1">13:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.1.1">Am 1:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.1.1">Mi 1:1</reference>). (<reference osisRef="2Cor.1.2">2</reference>) The point aimed at; the false "walking after their own spirit"; the true, after the Spirit of God. (3) The result; the false saw nothing, but spake as if they had seen; the true had a vision, not subjective, but objectively real [Fairbairn]. A refutation of those who set the inward word above the objective, and represent the Bible as flowing subjectively from the inner light of its writers, not from the revelation of the Holy Ghost from without. "They are impatient to get possession of the kernel without its fostering shell--they would have Christ without the Bible" [Bengel]. <div eID="gen20122" type="x-p"/>
entries.918b123337d96f8c43c56bca78cca6fc96dd0b2c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11162"/><div sID="gen20123" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11162"/><hi type="bold">4. foxes--</hi>which cunningly "spoil the vines" (<reference osisRef="Song.2.15">So 2:15</reference>), Israel being the vineyard (<reference osisRef="Ps.80.8-Ps.80.15">Psa 80:8-15</reference>; Is 5:1-7; 27:2; <reference osisRef="Jer.2.21">Jr 2:21</reference>); their duty was to have guarded it from being spoiled, whereas they themselves spoiled it by corruptions.<div eID="gen20123" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20124" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in ... deserts--</hi>where there is nothing to eat; whence the foxes become so ravenous and crafty in their devices to get food. So the prophets wander in Israel, a moral desert, unrestrained, greedy of gain which they get by craft. <div eID="gen20124" type="x-p"/>
entries.94dc89be1b1f6fd418980d43e72eefc32af9787b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11163"/><div sID="gen20125" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11163"/><hi type="bold">5. not gone up into ... gaps--</hi>metaphor from breaches made in a wall, to which the defenders ought to betake themselves in order to repel the entrance of the foe. The breach is that made in the theocracy through the nation's sin; and, unless it be made up, the vengeance of God will break in through it. Those who would advise the people to repentance are the restorers of the breach (<reference osisRef="Ezek.22.30">Eze 22:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.106.23">Psa 106:23</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.106.30">30</reference>).<div eID="gen20125" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20126" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hedge--</hi>the law of God (<reference osisRef="Ps.80.12">Psa 80:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.5.2">Is 5:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.5.5">5</reference>); by violating it, the people stripped themselves of the fence of God's protection and lay exposed to the foe. The false prophets did not try to repair the evil by bringing back the people to the law with good counsels, or by checking the bad with reproofs. These two duties answer to the double office of defenders in case of a breach made in a wall: (1) To repair the breach from within; (2) To oppose the foe from without.<div eID="gen20126" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20127" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to stand--</hi>that is, that the city may "stand."<div eID="gen20127" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20128" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in ... day of ... Lord--</hi>In the day of the battle which God wages against Israel for their sins, ye do not try to stay God's vengeance by prayers, and by leading the nation to repentance. <div eID="gen20128" type="x-p"/>
entries.3b2e47ea53ce7164a9a4419abcceb174953c5f1e: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11164"/><div sID="gen20129" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11164"/><hi type="bold">6. made others to hope, &c.--</hi>rather, "they hoped" to confirm (that is, 'make good') their word, by the event corresponding to their prophecy. The Hebrew requires this [Havernick]. Also the parallel clause, "they have seen vanity," implies that they believed their own lie (<reference osisRef="2Thess.2.11">2Th 2:11</reference>). Subjective revelation is false unless it rests on the objective. <div eID="gen20129" type="x-p"/>
entries.655b84eb18652f0b1b98b4463e333920b2304b76: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11165"/><div sID="gen20130" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11165"/><hi type="bold">8. I am against you--</hi>rather understand, "I come against you," to punish your wicked profanation of My name (compare <reference osisRef="Rev.2.5">Re 2:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.16">16</reference>). <div eID="gen20130" type="x-p"/>
entries.10ebf0e2f9e468113683ea570c3bb1fc793f5a0d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11166"/><div sID="gen20131" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11166"/><hi type="bold">9. mine hand--</hi>My power in vengeance.<div eID="gen20131" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20132" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not ... in ... assembly--</hi>rather, the "council"; "They shall not occupy the honorable office of councillors in the senate of elders after the return from Babylon" (<reference osisRef="Ezra.2.1">Ezr 2:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.2">2</reference>).<div eID="gen20132" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20133" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">neither ... written in ... Israel--</hi>They shall not even have a place in the register kept of all citizens' names; they shall be erased from it, just as the names of those who died in the year, or had been deprived of citizenship for their crimes, were at the annual revisal erased. Compare <reference osisRef="Jer.17.13">Jr 17:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.10.20">Lu 10:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.3.5">Re 3:5</reference>, as to those spiritually Israelites; <reference osisRef="John.1.47">Joh 1:47</reference>, and those not so. Literally fulfilled (<reference osisRef="Ezra.2.59">Ezr 2:59</reference>, 62; compare <reference osisRef="Neh.7.5">Ne 7:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.69.28">Psa 69:28</reference>).<div eID="gen20133" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20134" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">neither ... enter ... land--</hi>They shall not so much as be allowed to come back at all to their country. <div eID="gen20134" type="x-p"/>
entries.df8009678367adaa45149b89bb0f6f4a2476c0da: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11167"/><div sID="gen20135" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11167"/><hi type="bold">10. Because, even because--</hi>The repetition heightens the emphasis.<div eID="gen20135" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20136" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Peace--</hi>safety to the nation. Ezekiel confirms <reference osisRef="Jer.6.14">Jr 6:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.8.11">8:11</reference>.<div eID="gen20136" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20137" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">one--</hi>literally, "this one"; said contemptuously, as in <reference osisRef="2Chr.28.22">2Ch 28:22</reference>.<div eID="gen20137" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20138" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">a wall--</hi>rather, "a loose wall." Ezekiel had said that the false prophets did not "go up into the gaps, or make up the breaches" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.5">Eze 13:5</reference>), as good architects do; now he adds that they make a bustling show of anxiety about repairing the wall; but it is without right mortar, and therefore of no use.<div eID="gen20138" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20139" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">one ... others--</hi>besides individual effort, they jointly co-operated to delude the people.<div eID="gen20139" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20140" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">daubed ... with untempered mortar--</hi>as sand without lime, mud without straw [Grotius]. Fairbairn translates, "plaster it with whitewash." But besides the hypocrisy of merely outwardly "daubing" to make the wall look fair (<reference osisRef="Matt.23.27">Mt 23:27</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.23.29">29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.23.3">Ac 23:3</reference>), there is implied the unsoundness of the wall from the absence of true uniting cement; the "untempered cement" answering to the lie of the prophets, who say, in support of their prophecies, "Thus saith the Lord, when the Lord hath not spoken" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.22.28">Eze 22:28</reference>). <div eID="gen20140" type="x-p"/>
entries.1487325ebecffecaeba255674a3dc3637dfc1a93: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11168"/><div sID="gen20141" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11168"/><hi type="bold">11. overflowing--</hi>inundating; such as will at once wash away the mere clay mortar. The three most destructive agents shall co-operate against the wall--wind, rain, and hailstones. These last in the East are more out of the regular course of nature and are therefore often particularly specified as the instruments of God's displeasure against His foes (<reference osisRef="Exod.9.18">Ex 9:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.10.11">Jos 10:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.38.22">Job 38:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.18.12">Psa 18:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.18.13">13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.28.2">Is 28:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.30.30">30:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.16.21">Re 16:21</reference>). The Hebrew here is, literally, "stones of ice." They fall in Palestine at times an inch thick with a destructive velocity. The personification heightens the vivid effect, "O ye hail stones." The Chaldeans will be the violent agency whereby God will unmask and refute them, overthrowing their edifice of lies. <div eID="gen20141" type="x-p"/>
entries.0458157b18f49730937ab62c2940b0b5ab4e0fa6: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11169"/><div sID="gen20142" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11169"/><hi type="bold">12. shall it not be said--</hi>Your vanity and folly shall be so manifested that it shall pass into a proverb, "Where is the daubing?" <div eID="gen20142" type="x-p"/>
entries.ad240a1e66a3f9a0899fa9690850bcfc1fdb0153: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11170"/><div sID="gen20143" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11170"/>13. God repeats, in His own name, as the Source of the coming calamity, what had been expressed generally in <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.11">Eze 13:11</reference>. <div eID="gen20143" type="x-p"/>
entries.2fb1dcc711f65fc6cb40fae8f4dd30903a3d35e5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11171"/><div sID="gen20144" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11171"/>14. The repetition of the same threat (see on <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.11">Eze 13:11</reference>) is to awaken the people out of their dream of safety by the certainty of the event.<div eID="gen20144" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20145" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">foundation--</hi>As the "wall" represents the security of the nation, so the "foundation" is Jerusalem, on the fortifications of which they rested their confidence. Grotius makes the "foundation" refer to the false principles on which they rested; <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.16">Eze 13:16</reference> supports the former view. <div eID="gen20145" type="x-p"/>
entries.df04e570b3d97481bcdad49b185bfb4b69eaa3c7: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11172"/><div sID="gen20146" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11172"/><hi type="bold">16. prophesy concerning Jerusalem--</hi>With all their "seeing visions of peace for her," they cannot ensure peace or safety to themselves. <div eID="gen20146" type="x-p"/>
entries.2aca7941cca680789b001d2dd23428f5177c87ba: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11173"/><div sID="gen20147" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11173"/><hi type="bold">17. set thy face--</hi>put on a bold countenance, fearlessly to denounce them (<reference osisRef="Ezek.3.8">Eze 3:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.3.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.50.7">Is 50:7</reference>).<div eID="gen20147" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20148" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">daughters--</hi>the false prophetesses; alluded to only here; elsewhere the guilt specified in the women is the active share they took in maintaining idolatry (<reference osisRef="Ezek.8.14">Eze 8:14</reference>). It was only in extraordinary emergencies that God bestowed prophecy on women, for example on Miriam, Deborah, Huldah (<reference osisRef="Exod.15.20">Ex 15:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Judg.4.4">Jud 4:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.22.14">2Ki 22:14</reference>); so in the last days to come (<reference osisRef="Joel.2.28">Joe 2:28</reference>). The rareness of such instances enhanced their guilt in pretending inspiration. <div eID="gen20148" type="x-p"/>
entries.399b34816c47336cdbddb952d5df50c2efbbbf73: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11174"/><div sID="gen20149" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11174"/><hi type="bold">18. sew pillows to ... armholes--</hi>rather, elbows and wrists, for which the false prophetesses made cushions to lean on, as a symbolical act, typifying the perfect tranquility which they foretold to those consulting them. Perhaps they made their dupes rest on these cushions in a fancied state of ecstasy after they had made them at first stand (whence the expression, "every stature," is used for "men of every age"). As the men are said to have built a wall (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.10">Eze 13:10</reference>), so the women are said to sew pillows, &c., both alike typifying the "peace" they promised the impenitent.<div eID="gen20149" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20150" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">make kerchiefs--</hi>magical veils, which they put over the heads of those consulting them, as if to fit them for receiving a response, that they might be rapt in spiritual trance above the world.<div eID="gen20150" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20151" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">head of every stature--</hi>"men of every age," old and young, great and small, if only these had pay to offer them.<div eID="gen20151" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20152" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hunt souls--</hi>eagerly trying to allure them to the love of yourselves (<reference osisRef="Prov.6.26">Pr 6:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Pet.2.14">2Pe 2:14</reference>), so as unwarily to become your prey.<div eID="gen20152" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20153" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">will ye save ... souls ... that come unto you--</hi>Will ye haul after souls, and when they are yours ("come unto you"), will ye promise them life? "Save" is explained (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.22">Eze 13:22</reference>), "promising life" [Grotius]. Calvin explains, "Will ye hunt My people's souls and yet will ye save your own souls"; I, the Lord God, will not allow it. But "save" is used (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.19">Eze 13:19</reference>) of the false prophetesses promising life to the impenitent, so that English Version and Grotius explain it best. <div eID="gen20153" type="x-p"/>
entries.fc04f78cc052e10cba149ef87a8c540184e764e3: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11175"/><div sID="gen20154" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11175"/><hi type="bold">19. handfuls--</hi>expressing the paltry gain for which they bartered immortal souls (compare <reference osisRef="Mic.3.5">Mi 3:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.3.11">11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.12.16">He 12:16</reference>). They "polluted" God by making His name the cloak under which they uttered falsehoods.<div eID="gen20154" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20155" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">among my people--</hi>an aggravation of their sin, that they committed it "among the people" whom God had chosen as peculiarly His own, and among whom He had His temple. It would have been a sin to have done so even among the Gentiles, who knew not God; much more so among the people of God (compare <reference osisRef="Prov.28.21">Pr 28:21</reference>).<div eID="gen20155" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20156" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">slay ... souls that should not die, &c.--</hi>to predict the slaying or perdition of the godly whom I will save. As true ministers are said to save and slay their hearers, according to the spirit respectively in which these receive their message (<reference osisRef="2Cor.2.15">2Co 2:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.16">16</reference>), so false ministers imitate them; but they promise safety to those on the broad way to ruin and predict ruin to those on the narrow way of God.<div eID="gen20156" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20157" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my people that hear your lies--</hi>who are therefore wilfully deceived, so that their guilt lies at their own door (<reference osisRef="John.3.19">Joh 3:19</reference>). <div eID="gen20157" type="x-p"/>
entries.298f0a95f152cc6a6b7ebb9689f232c91d63922f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11176"/><div sID="gen20158" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11176"/><hi type="bold">20. I am against your pillows--</hi>that is, against your lying ceremonial tricks by which ye cheat the people.<div eID="gen20158" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20159" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to make them fly--</hi>namely, into their snares, as fowlers disturb birds so as to be suddenly caught in the net spread for them. "Fly" is peculiarly appropriate as to those lofty spiritual flights to which they pretended to raise their dupes when they veiled their heads with kerchiefs and made them rest on luxurious arm-cushions (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.18">Eze 13:18</reference>).<div eID="gen20159" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20160" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">let ... souls go--</hi>"Ye make them fly" in order to destroy them; "I will let them go" in order to save them (<reference osisRef="Ps.91.3">Psa 91:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.6.5">Pr 6:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.9.8">Ho 9:8</reference>). <div eID="gen20160" type="x-p"/>
entries.423060b3d505728bfd2b115e9453c8a6ba5db880: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11177"/><div sID="gen20161" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11177"/><hi type="bold">21. in your hand--</hi>in your power. "My people" are the elect remnant of Israel to be saved.<div eID="gen20161" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20162" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ye shall know--</hi>by the judgments which ye shall suffer. <div eID="gen20162" type="x-p"/>
entries.1b2446f97d27484bc080e839367c2e4df268a9b5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11178"/><div sID="gen20163" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11178"/><hi type="bold">22. ye have made ... the righteous sad--</hi>by lying predictions of calamities impending ever the godly.<div eID="gen20163" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20164" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">strengthened ... wicked--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Jer.23.14">Jr 23:14</reference>).<div eID="gen20164" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20165" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heart of ... righteous ... hands of ... wicked--</hi>Heart is applied to the righteous because the terrors foretold penetrated to their inmost feelings; hands, to the wicked because they were so hardened as not only to despise God in their minds, but also to manifest it in their whole acts, as if avowedly waging war with Him. <div eID="gen20165" type="x-p"/>
entries.1c2757d5d824acfad03d2eb43890ca0894eb8851: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11179"/><div sID="gen20166" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11179"/><hi type="bold">23. ye shall see no more vanity--</hi>The event shall confute your lies, involving yourselves in destruction (<reference osisRef="Ezek.13.9">Eze 13:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.14.8">Eze 14:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.15.7">15:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.3.6">Mi 3:6</reference>). <chapter eID="Ezek.13"/>

entries.934dcadb45dddcb3a22871a6bcc59730dfbbd8f0: <div eID="gen31506" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen31507" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen31508" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen31508" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen31507" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen31509" type="x-p"/> This chapter denounces heavy judgments against the lying prophets who flattered the people, in the midst of their sin and danger, with false hopes of peace and security, <reference osisRef="Eze.13.1-Eze.13.9">Eze 13:1-9</reference>. The work of these deceivers is beautifully compared to a frail and insolent piece of building, which can never stand against the battering elements of heaven, (the Chaldean forces), which God will commission against it, <reference osisRef="Eze.13.10-Eze.13.16">Eze 13:10-16</reference>. In the remaining part of the chapter woes are denounced against false prophetesses who practiced vain rites and divinations, with the view of promoting their own gain by deceiving the people, <reference osisRef="Eze.13.17-Eze.13.23">Eze 13:17-23</reference>.
entries.c91caae0e835f332c399be1ecd87ebe84049f265: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen31509" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31510" type="x-p"/> That prophesy out of their own hearts - Who are neither inspired nor sent by Me. They are prophets out of their own hearts. They have their mission from their own assumption, and proceed in it from their own presumption. Such either go of themselves, or are sent by man. Such prophets, ministers, preachers, and clergy have been a curse to the Church and to the world for some thousands of years.
entries.93798cf66d32b780dc7c1f41cee61c701efbd43c: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen31510" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31511" type="x-p"/> Thy prophets are like the foxes in the deserts - The cunning of the fox in obtaining his prey has been long proverbial. These false prophets are represented as the foxes who, having got their prey by great subtlety, run to the desert to hide both themselves and it. So the false prophets, when the event did not answer to their prediction, got out of the way, that they might not be overwhelmed with the reproaches and indignation of the people.
entries.a68cb56e329ca3fa641440faf37fa0cb97112677: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen31511" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31512" type="x-p"/> Ye have not gone up into the gaps - Far from opposing sinners, who are bringing down the wrath of God upon the place, you prevent their repentance by your flattering promises and false predictions. Ye have neither by prayers, example, nor advice, contributed any thing for the preservation of the place, or the salvation of the people's souls.
entries.3e3d540050509a86f39f63ac5aa3668750d7d496: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen31512" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31513" type="x-p"/> They shall not be in the assembly of my people - They shall not be reputed members of my Church. They shall not be reckoned in the genealogy of true Israelites that return from captivity; and they shall never have a possession in the land; they shall be exhereditated and expatriated. They shall all perish in the siege, by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence.
entries.208d0ed2395f1251f4f55a4f2935899732ef13b3: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen31513" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31514" type="x-p"/> One built up a wall - A true prophet is as a wall of defense to the people. These false prophets pretend to be a wall of defense; but their wall is bad, and their mortar is worse. One gives a lying vision, another pledges himself that it is true; and the people believe what they say, and trust not in God, nor turn from their sins. The city is about to be besieged; it needs stronger fortifications than what it possesses. The prophet should be as a brazen wall for its defense; and such my prophets would have been had the people received the word from my mouth. But ye have prevented this by your lying vanities; and when you have perverted the people, you pretend to raise up a rampart of specious prophecy, full of fine promises, for their defense. What one false prophet says, another confirms; and this is like daubing over a bad wall with bad mortar, which prevents its blemishes and weaknesses being discovered, though it has no tendency to strengthen the building.
entries.183e07619d1588acdcc122e4ab30d3e92ab0a929: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen31514" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31515" type="x-p"/> There shall be an overflowing shower - That shall wash off this bad mortar; sweep away the ground on which the wall stands, and level it with the earth. In the eastern countries, where the walls are built with unbaked bricks, desolations of this kind are often occasioned by tempestuous rains. Of this sort of materials were the walls of ancient cities made, and hence the reason why no vestige of them remains. Witness Babylon, which was thus built. See the note on <reference osisRef="Eze.4.1">Eze 4:1</reference>.
entries.4f637a36c50fbd257310556bd08c08b6d7b377fd: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen31515" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31516" type="x-p"/> Set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesy - From this it appears that there were prophetesses in the land of Israel, that were really inspired by the Lord: for as a false religion necessarily implies a true one, of which it is the ape; so false prophetesses necessarily imply true ones, whom they endeavored to imitate. <div eID="gen31516" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31517" type="x-p"/> That there were true prophetesses among the Jews is evident enough from such being mentioned in the sacred writings. Miriam, the sister of Moses <reference osisRef="Exo.15.20">Exo 15:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Num.12.2">Num 12:2</reference>; Deborah, <reference osisRef="Jdg.4.4">Jdg 4:4</reference>; Huldah, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.22.14">2Kgs 22:14</reference>; Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, <reference osisRef="Luk.2.36">Luk 2:36</reference>; the four daughters of Philip the deacon, <reference osisRef="Act.21.9">Act 21:9</reference>. <div eID="gen31517" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31518" type="x-p"/> Calmet observes that there was scarcely a heresy in the primitive Church that was not supported and fomented by seducing women.
entries.d2fea358f6146b6f99e0b8d3857449ceb065083d: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen31518" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31519" type="x-p"/> That sew pillows to all arm holes - I believe this refers to those cushions which are so copiously provided in the eastern countries for the apartments of women; on which they sit, lean, rest their heads, and prop up their arms. I have several drawings of eastern ladies, who are represented on sofas; and often with their arm thrown over a pillow, which is thereby pressed close to their side, and against which they thus recline. The prophet's discourse seems to point out that state of softness and effeminacy to which the predictions of those false prophetesses allured the inhabitants of Jerusalem. A careless voluptuous life is that which is here particularly reprehended. <div eID="gen31519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31520" type="x-p"/> And make kerchiefs - The word kerchief is French, couvre chef, that which covers the head; hence handkerchief and neck handkerchief, and pocket handkerchief are pitifully improper; because none of them is used to cover the head, from which alone that article of dress has its name. But what are we to understand by kerchiefs here? Probably some kind of ornamental dress which rendered women more enticing, so that they could the more successfully hunt or inveigle souls (men) into the worship of their false gods. These they put on heads of every stature - women of all ages, קומה komah, of every woman that rose up to inveigle men to idolatry. <div eID="gen31520" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31521" type="x-p"/> The word מספחות mispachoth, translated here kerchiefs, and by the Vulgate cervicalia, bolsters, Calmet contends, means a sort of nets used in hunting, and in every place where it occurs it will bear this meaning; and hence the use to which it is here said to be applied, to hunt souls.
entries.542b0d4db7e5fa5792cc9739cf42ae8e23fd9cca: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen31521" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31522" type="x-p"/> The souls that ye hunt to make them fly - לפרחות lephorechoth, into the flower gardens, says Parkhurst. These false prophetesses decoyed men into these gardens, where probably some impure rites of worship were performed, as in that of אשרה Asherah or Venus. See Parkhurst under פרח.
entries.cfdfffb3086065684b3f1a01e9a4de8f6acc2a13: <hi type="bold">Verse 21</hi> <div eID="gen31522" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31523" type="x-p"/> Your kerchiefs - Nets, or amulets, as some think.
entries.91d694395a182383861bbfaee67fa672f9afb7e0: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen31523" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31524" type="x-p"/> With lies ye have made the heart of the righteous sad - Here is the ministry of these false prophetesses, and its effects. They told lies: they would speak, and they had no truth to tell; and therefore spoke falsities. They "saddened the souls of the righteous, and strengthened the hands of the wicked." They promised them life, and prevented them from repenting and turning from their sins.
entries.9bb72acb45e52a48e8d24fd96580749bc5e2b8af: <hi type="bold">Verse 23</hi> <div eID="gen31524" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31525" type="x-p"/> Ye shall see no more vanity - They pretended visions; but they were empty of reality. <div eID="gen31525" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31526" type="x-p"/> Nor divine divinations - As God would not speak to them, they employed demons. Where God is not, because of the iniquity of the people, the devil is, to strengthen and support that iniquity. And if he cannot have his priests, he will have his priestesses; and these will have a Church like themselves, full of lying doctrines, and bad works.  <chapter eID="Ezek.13"/> <div eID="gen31526" type="x-p"/>

entries.c9cba78fec5373f8bcdb66485e793140ac4ffea4: <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.1-Ezek.13.7">Eze 13:1-7</reference> <div eID="gen14884" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s2">Against the False Prophets</title> <div sID="gen14885" type="x-p"/> Their conduct. - Eze 13:1. <hi type="italic">And the word of Jehovah came to me, saying,</hi> Eze 13:2. <hi type="italic">Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy, and say to the prophets out of their heart, Hear ye the word of Jehovah.</hi> Eze 13:3. <hi type="italic">Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Woe upon the foolish prophets, who go after their spirit, and that which they have not seen!</hi> Eze 13:4. <hi type="italic">Like foxes in ruins have thy prophets become, O Israel.</hi> Eze 13:5. <hi type="italic">Ye do not stand before the breaches, nor wall up the wall around the house of Israel to stand firm in the battle on the day of Jehovah.</hi> Eze 13:6. <hi type="italic">They see vanity and lying soothsaying, who say, “Oracle of Jehovah;” and Jehovah hath not sent them; so that they might hope for the fulfilment of the word.</hi> Eze 13:7. <hi type="italic">Do ye not see vain visions, and speak lying soothsaying, and say, Oracle of Jehovah; and I have not spoken?</hi> - The addition  הנּבּאים, “who prophesy,” is not superfluous. Ezekiel is not to direct his words against the prophets as a body, but against those who follow the vocation of prophet in Israel without being called to it by God on receiving a divine revelation, but simply prophesying out of their own heart, or according to their own subjective imagination.
